rules.sentence: The nerve is typically compressed by the fibrous bands that often originate from the deep head of the brachialis fascia and the pronator teres, and this pressure can increase with minor variations.[9]

Anterior interosseous nerve syndrome should be clinically differentiated from stenosing tenosynovitis or pathologies limited to local pathology affecting the flexor tendons alone (ie, flexor tendon adhesions or partial versus complete flexor tendon rupture).
Compression distal to the anterior interosseous nerve branch point should have only selective FDP or FPL denervation.
There should be sensory involvement if the compression occurs proximal to the anterior interosseous nerve.
